html:
A sea battle in the narrow strait between the island of Salamis and the coast near Athens, in September 480 BCE. Xerxes had just burned Athens. Themistocles lured the larger Persian fleet into the strait, where its numbers counted for little, and the Greeks broke it.

Xerxes went home, and the land army he left behind was beaten at Plataea the next year. The win made the Athenian navy, and the rowers who manned it, the heart of the city's power. See athens-golden-age.
